facts.fact: Local cable TV advertising typically requires minimum commitments of often $1,000-5,000 per month, according to the Adwave guide.
Local cable TV commercial production costs are stated as $2,000-10,000 for a commercial.
Per the Adwave guide, streaming TV (CTV) lower minimums start at $30 a day with platforms like Adwave.
facts.quote: Lower minimums (start at $30 a day with [platforms like Adwave](https://adwave.com/pricing/))

facts.fact: Adwave states that streaming TV campaigns go live within 24 hours.
Adwave's guide budget table lists a solo operator monthly TV budget of $300-500.
facts.quote: | Solo operator | $300-500 | Local awareness, slow build |

facts.fact: Adwave's guide budget table lists a small team (2-5) monthly TV budget of $500-1,500.
facts.quote: | Small team (2-5) | $500-1,500 | Consistent presence, seasonal spikes |

facts.fact: Adwave's guide budget table lists an established company (5-15) monthly TV budget of $1,500-5,000.
Adwave's guide budget table lists a large operation (15+) monthly TV budget of $5,000 or more.
facts.quote: | Large operation (15+) | $5,000+ | Full coverage, brand campaigns |

facts.fact: The guide says many home service businesses allocate 5-10% of revenue to marketing, with TV possibly representing 20-30% of that marketing budget.
facts.value: 5-10% of revenue; TV 20-30% of marketing budget
facts.quote: Many home service businesses allocate 5-10% of revenue to marketing. TV might represent 20-30% of that marketing budget

facts.fact: In the guide's worked example, a plumbing company with $500,000 annual revenue has a monthly TV budget of $400-1,250.
The guide's example targeting for an HVAC company uses a 25-mile radius around the main office and household income of $75,000+.
The guide suggests targeting homeowners aged 35 and up, since that age group typically makes household maintenance decisions.
Streaming TV (CTV) is described as offering precise geographic targeting down to ZIP code.
facts.quote: Precise geographic targeting (down to ZIP code)

facts.fact: For a heating-focused HVAC company, the guide suggests allocating 50% of the annual TV budget to October through February.
For a heating-focused HVAC company, the guide suggests allocating 25% of the annual TV budget to March through May.
For a heating-focused HVAC company, the guide suggests allocating 25% of the annual TV budget to June through September.
The guide states that good TV campaign results for home service businesses include phone calls increasing 10-30% during TV campaigns.
facts.quote: Phone calls increase 10-30% during TV campaigns

facts.fact: In the Phoenix-area HVAC case example, the company spent $1,200/month on streaming TV targeting homeowners within 20 miles.
facts.quote: spent $1,200/month on streaming TV targeting homeowners within 20 miles

facts.fact: In the Phoenix-area HVAC case example, the company increased streaming TV spend to $2,000/month during summer peak.
facts.quote: During summer peak, they increased to $2,000/month.

facts.fact: In the Phoenix-area HVAC case example, inbound calls increased 35% after one year of streaming TV advertising.
In the suburban Chicago plumbing case example, the company allocated $800/month to streaming TV.
In the Texas roofing case example, the company maintained a $500/month baseline TV presence.
The guide suggests a reasonable starting budget for testing CTV advertising is $500 to $1,000 per month.
facts.quote: A reasonable starting budget for testing CTV is $500 to $1,000 per month

facts.fact: The guide states that established home services businesses often allocate 5 to 10 percent of their marketing budget to TV advertising.
facts.quote: Established home services businesses often allocate 5 to 10 percent of their marketing budget to TV advertising.
